sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from $1.70 billion in FY2016 to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The FY2020 step change, revenue up 49.1% [D194], came from the U.S. launch of TRIKAFTA in the fourth quarter of 2019 and KAFTRIO in the EU in the third quarter of 2020 [P51].
Growth then decelerated to 8.9% in FY2025 [D446], with net product revenues up $950.5 million, or 9%, on continued demand [P3].
The window is a launch-driven ramp, not a cycle: operating margin swung from 0.6% in FY2016 to a 48.2% high in FY2022 and back to 34.8% in FY2025 [F26][F32][F35].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO contributed 29.5pp of the 22.1% revenue growth in FY2021 and 26.3pp in FY2022 [D519][D247][D522][D300].
Its share of revenue peaked at 92.9% in FY2024 and fell to 85.9% in FY2025 as ALYFTREK launched [D526][D529].
ALYFTREK added 7.6pp of FY2025 growth on $837.8 million of sales, while TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO added only 0.7pp [D590][S69][D531].

Operating income grew far faster than revenue over the window, at a 95.6% CAGR against 24.2% [F197][F196], but the FY2025 incremental margin of 449.1% [D463] reflects recovery from the FY2024 loss, not new leverage.
Diluted EPS rose to $15.32 in FY2025 from $13.89 in FY2023 [F75][F73] while the diluted share count was flat at 258.0 million [X137][D459].
FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% [F35] sits above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high [D663][D662].
The FY2024 collapse to -2.1% [F34] came from $4.6 billion of AIPR&D, including $4.4 billion for Alpine [P11], and SG&A up 29% on launch preparation [P6].
In FY2025 the margin recovered 36.9pp [D452], with SG&A costing 1.3pp and R&D adding 0.4pp [D467][D466].
Cost of revenue held at 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D425] as a lower overall royalty rate for CF medicines offset other costs [P4].
Net margin of 32.9% [F55] trailed operating margin of 34.8% [F35], with the 14.9% effective tax rate [D433] close to the 17.4% FY2023 level [D339].
Operating cash flow was $3.63 billion in FY2025, primarily from $4.17 billion of operating income [F85][F25][P1].
Free cash flow of $3.19 billion was a 26.6% margin [F105][D431], below the 32.8% window median [D669], and free cash flow covered net income only 0.81x against a 1.07x median [D435][D675].
Capex rose 47.0% to $437.6 million, 3.6% of revenue and 2.09x D&A [D447][F95][D430][D436].
Days inventory outstanding climbed to 373 days from 287 [D444][D397], and stock-based compensation was 18.9% of operating cash flow [D437].
Cash and investments of $12.3 billion [D438] equal 102.7% of revenue, the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers against a -50.7% median [D440][D691][D692].
The FY2024 dip to $11.2 billion [D392] came from the Alpine acquisition and buybacks [P10], and FY2025 rebuilt it on product revenue [P2].
Buybacks of $2.02 billion were 63.2% of free cash flow in FY2025 [D441][D442], yet the diluted share count was unchanged [D459].
Return on average equity of 22.5% [D445] ranked in the 38th percentile of eight peers against a 38.7% median [D695][D696].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days in FY2025 to 373 [R1][D444][D397], far above the 156 days of FY2022 [D298]; the filings cited do not explain the build.
Free cash flow conversion of 0.81x net income [D435] sits in the 14th percentile of seven peers against a 1.11x median [D693][D694], a persistent gap from working-capital absorption.
The effective tax rate moved -300.7pp in FY2025 [R2][D433][D390] because the FY2024 rate reflected non-deductible Alpine AIPR&D [P5], so the swing is a base effect, not a new benefit.
FY2019 buybacks were later restated to $186.0 million from $192.0 million [R3][X141], a data-quality note that does not affect any conclusion here.

If TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth stays below the 0.7pp contribution of FY2025 [D531], ALYFTREK must keep adding near its 7.6pp [D590] for revenue growth to hold above the 10.4% three-year CAGR [D679]; watch the FY2026 10-K product table.
A further rise in days inventory outstanding above 373 days [D444] without matching revenue growth would confirm the working-capital drag; watch the FY2026 10-K balance sheet.
Operating margin falling back below the 31.8% window median [D663] would reverse the FY2025 recovery; watch the FY2026 10-K income statement.
